title: How to Reach Chitwan from Kathmandu, Pokhara and India
meta_description: How to reach Chitwan from Kathmandu, Pokhara and India: flights to Bharatpur, tourist buses, private cars, Raxaul and Sunauli border routes, times and costs.
summary: Chitwan is 165 km from Kathmandu (5–7 h by road or a 25-minute flight to Bharatpur), 150 km from Pokhara (5–6 h by road) and 4–5 hours from the Indian border at Raxaul–Birgunj or Sunauli–Bhairahawa. Tourist buses are cheapest, private cars most flexible, and flights fastest.

sections.heading: Chitwan routes at a glance
paras: Most visitors stay in Sauraha on the north-east edge of the park, so times below are to Sauraha. Patihani and Jagatpur, near the park headquarters, are about the same distance; Meghauli in the west adds about an hour from Bharatpur. Road times assume good conditions and include a short meal stop; road works on the Mugling–Narayangarh stretch and monsoon landslides can add hours.

sections.heading: From Kathmandu by air
paras: Bharatpur Airport is Chitwan's airport, about 15 km from Sauraha. Buddha Air and Yeti/Tara Air fly from Kathmandu several times a day, taking about 25 minutes, with views of the Mahabharat hills and, on clear days, the Himalaya to the north. Fares for foreigners are typically around US$ 110–130 one way; Nepali and Indian nationals pay less. Hotels and our packages include the airport transfer, 30 minutes to Sauraha or Patihani and about an hour to Meghauli.

Flying is the best choice for seniors, families with young children, short trips and luxury stays in Meghauli. The main drawback is weather: from mid-December to January, morning fog in the Terai often delays the first flights, so book late-morning or afternoon departures in winter. Checked baggage is usually limited to about 20 kg on domestic flights; check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: From Kathmandu by road
paras: The road leaves Kathmandu at Kalanki, climbs over the valley rim at Nagdhunga, and drops via Naubise into the Trishuli gorge. It follows the river past Malekhu, Charaudi and Kurintar, the Manakamana cable car base, to Mugling, then turns south along the Trishuli to Narayangarh and east to Tandi and Sauraha. It is about 165 km, all paved, but busy with trucks and buses.

A private car takes 5–6 hours plus stops and lets you add Manakamana, rafting at Charaudi or Devghat. Tourist buses leave the Kantipath and Thamel area around 7 am, stop for breakfast and lunch, and reach the Sauraha bus park around 1–2 pm. Check that your bus goes into Sauraha rather than stopping at Tandi on the highway. Local buses are cheaper but slow and crowded.
list: Leave by 7:30 am to clear Kalanki before traffic builds
Allow extra time for road works between Mugling and Narayangarh
Take motion-sickness tablets for the winding gorge section
Avoid driving at night on this route

sections.heading: From Pokhara
paras: Pokhara to Sauraha is about 150 km, 5–6 hours, via Damauli and Mugling, then down the Trishuli to Narayangarh. Tourist buses leave Pokhara's Tourist Bus Park around 7:30 am and arrive in Sauraha in the early afternoon. A private car is quicker and allows a stop at Bandipur, the old Newar hill town above Dumre, which makes a good lunch break.

There are no scheduled flights between Pokhara and Bharatpur, so road is the only practical option. Many travellers do a loop: Kathmandu to Pokhara, Pokhara to Chitwan, and fly or drive back to Kathmandu from Chitwan. Others continue from Chitwan to Lumbini and exit to India at Sunauli.

sections.heading: From India overland
paras: Two border crossings put Chitwan within a day of India. Raxaul (Bihar) to Birgunj is the closest: from Birgunj the road runs north via Pathlaiya and Hetauda, then west to Tandi and Sauraha, about 150 km and 4–5 hours. Raxaul has trains from Kolkata, Delhi and other cities. Sunauli (Uttar Pradesh) to Bhairahawa suits travellers coming from Gorakhpur, Varanasi or Lucknow: from Bhairahawa it is about 165 km and 4–5 hours east via Butwal and Narayangarh, and Lumbini is only 22 km from Bhairahawa.

Indian citizens cross with a passport or voter ID card and do not need a visa; third-country nationals need a Nepal visa, available on arrival at these borders, and should check current rules. Indian-registered vehicles need a customs permit, called bhansar, issued at the border for a daily fee. Our drivers can meet you at the Nepal side of either border.

sections.heading: From India by air
paras: Most Indian travellers fly into Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu from Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Kolkata or Varanasi, then continue to Chitwan by a domestic flight to Bharatpur or by road. Return economy fares from Delhi usually range from ₹12,000 to ₹25,000 depending on season and booking time. Allow at least three hours between arriving in Kathmandu and a domestic flight, as you must collect bags and move to the domestic terminal.

Gautam Buddha International Airport at Bhairahawa, near Lumbini, also handles some international and domestic flights. When international flights operate there, it can be a convenient gateway for a Lumbini and Chitwan trip; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the best way to reach Chitwan from Kathmandu?
faqs.a: For speed and comfort, fly to Bharatpur in about 25 minutes and drive 30 minutes to Sauraha. For flexibility, take a private car, 5–6 hours with stops at places like Manakamana or Devghat. On a budget, the tourist bus takes 6–7 hours and costs NPR 800–1,200 per seat.

faqs.q: How far is Chitwan from Kathmandu?
faqs.a: About 165 km by road to Sauraha via Mugling and Narayangarh, which takes 5–7 hours. The flight to Bharatpur covers the distance in about 25 minutes. Meghauli, in west Chitwan, is about 190 km by road.

faqs.q: How do I get from Pokhara to Chitwan?
faqs.a: By road, about 150 km and 5–6 hours via Damauli and Mugling. Tourist buses leave Pokhara around 7:30 am. A private car is quicker and can stop at Bandipur. There are no regular flights between Pokhara and Bharatpur.

faqs.q: Which Indian border is closest to Chitwan?
faqs.a: Raxaul–Birgunj, about 150 km and 4–5 hours from Sauraha via Hetauda. Sunauli–Bhairahawa is about 165 km and 4–5 hours via Butwal and suits travellers combining Chitwan with Lumbini. Both are open to Indian citizens; third-country nationals should check current entry rules.

faqs.q: Is there a direct bus from India to Chitwan?
faqs.a: Some private operators run buses from Indian cities such as Delhi and Varanasi to Kathmandu and Pokhara via the border, and travellers can get off at Narayangarh. More commonly, people travel to Raxaul or Sunauli, cross on foot or by rickshaw, and take a Nepali bus or car onward.

faqs.q: Can I drive my Indian car to Chitwan?
faqs.a: Yes. Indian-registered vehicles can enter Nepal with a customs permit, bhansar, issued at the border for a daily fee. Carry the registration certificate, insurance and driving licence. Nepal drives on the left, like India. Check current permit rules before you travel.

faqs.q: Is the Kathmandu to Chitwan flight worth it?
faqs.a: Yes if you are short on time, travelling with seniors or young children, or staying in Meghauli. It saves about five hours each way. In December and January, morning fog can delay flights, so book later departures. For budget trips, the tourist bus is good value.

faqs.q: How long is the drive from Lumbini to Chitwan?
faqs.a: About 165 km and 4.5–5 hours by car via Bhairahawa, Butwal and Narayangarh on the flat Mahendra Highway. Tourist buses take 5–6 hours. There are no direct flights between Bhairahawa and Bharatpur.

faqs.q: Is the road to Chitwan safe in the monsoon?
faqs.a: It stays open most of the time, but landslides occasionally block the Trishuli section between Kathmandu and Mugling from June to September, causing delays of hours. Travel in daylight, allow extra time, and consider flying if your schedule is tight.
